newsitem.title: UK: EBRD says Q1'97 provisions increased significantly.
newsitem.headline: EBRD says Q1'97 provisions increased significantly.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said operating profits in the first quarter of 1997 rose by one third from the same period last year though higher provisions resulted in a net loss.

Following an increase in provisioning, which is consistent with the EBRD's prudent provision policy, the bank reported a loss of 7.9 million Ecu for the first quarter compared with a loss of 0.70 million Ecu in the first quarter of 1996.

"The outlook for 1997 remains cautiously positive. Our first-quarter results are in keeping with previous experience. We are committed to continuing our prudent provisioning policy to deal immediately with any increase in credit risk in the region," Bart le Blanc, vice president of finance at the EBRD, told a news conference.
"Provisions are 70 percent higher than the first quarter of 1996 and there are a number of factors accountable for that," Le Blanc further told reporters.
nal factors, coupled with increased volume in the bank's portfolio and risks in credit quality, accounted for the increased provisions.
"First quarters at the EBRD are always difficult...and that is due to a combination of seasonal factors," le Blanc added.

"We always have lower income in the first quarter...and that is the result of the fact we have a significant equity portfolio and income from the...portfolio is not spread over the year as is from a loan portfolio, where you get interest from and fees and comminssion income on a regular basis," he added.
Le Blanc said dividends from the equity portfolio are usually never declared in the first quarter.
In addition, le Blanc said costs in first quarters are normally a bit higher than other quarters because of costs associated with the bank's annual meeting and its staff bonuses.
"That is the structural seasonality in the P&L (profit and loss)," Le Blanc said.
On the positive side, Le Blanc emphasised that the bank's income was significantly higher than last year and income from banking and treasury activities increased by almost one-third.
"Costs have been very much kept under control and as a result our operating profit is one third higher than it was last year," Le Blanc said.
Profits before provisions, which were in line with earlier projections, were 24.0 million Ecu in the first quarter compared with 18.06 million Ecu for the same period a year earlier.
Eleven projects were signed in the first quarter, with a value of 373.1 million Ecu. This compares with 16 projects in the same period last year, worth 340.2 million Ecu.
Project disbursements were 306.3 million Ecu, almost 14 percent higher than in the first quarter of 1996.
At the end of March 1997, the EBRD had committed a cumulative total of 8.34 billion Ecu to projects in its 26 countries of operations and net disbursements amounted to 3.41 billion Ecu.
